advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Count verdict-less/None sidecars into an explicit bucket (or reject) rather than a silent None/"null" key in verdict_histogram.
evidence: corpus.py:270: `"verdict": data.get("verdict")` — None when the key is absent
A sidecar missing `verdict` produces a None key that json.dumps(sort_keys=True) coerces to "null"; the count is indistinguishable from a legitimate verdict named 'null'.
advisory.finding: verdict_histogram is keyed directly on row["verdict"], which is data.get("verdict") and may be None when a sidecar omits the verdict; a None/absent verdict is silently bucketed (json.dumps coerces the None key to "null") rather than being counted as malformed, so a sidecar with no verdict is invisible in the histogram.
scenarios: A plan_review_result sidecar in history that lacks a verdict field is rolled into a 'null' bucket instead of being flagged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with `reviewed_related_material` containing a `role=='child'` entry (plus a non-child / missing-canonical_id entry) that verifies children are extracted and folded into the reconstructed fingerprint.
evidence: corpus.py:234-237: `item["canonical_id"] for item in reviewed_related_material if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("role") == "child" and item.get("canonical_id")`
All tests set `"reviewed_related_material": []` (e.g. test_plan_replay_corpus.py review_result data blocks) — no child entry is ever supplied.
ABSENCE: no test verifies a sidecar with child material reconstructs/verifies, nor that non-child roles or missing canonical_id are filtered out.
advisory.finding: No test exercises `_child_ids` child-material extraction: the added `_child_ids` filter (role=='child', canonical_id present) and the children path into the reconstructed PlanContext are never driven — every test passes `reviewed_related_material: []`. A regression in child parsing or in folding children into the fingerprint would not be caught.
scenarios: A refactor or regression in child extraction (role/canonical_id filtering) silently breaks fingerprint verification for tickets with children.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that builds a `plan_review_result_v1` sidecar and asserts it is enumerated and counted in schema_histogram.
evidence: manifest schema_histogram initialized with both schemas.
ABSENCE: all test review_result payloads use `"schema": "plan_review_result_v2"`; no v1 sidecar is ever built or asserted in schema_histogram.
advisory.finding: The `plan_review_result_v1` schema acceptance and histogram counting (added to `_SCHEMAS`) is untested — every test uses only `plan_review_result_v2`.
scenarios: A regression that drops v1 from `_SCHEMAS` (or mis-counts v1) would pass CI.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compute the empty-material fingerprint live (`material_fingerprint(_ctx(ticket_id, ""))`) and assert the stored sidecar fingerprint equals it before asserting the row is unverified, so the anti-spurious-match guard is actually exercised.
evidence: test line 406: `empty_material_fingerprint = "3be6beba619b59e5"` with a comment claiming it is `material_fingerprint()` of empty material, but no live `material_fingerprint(empty_ctx) == empty_material_fingerprint` assertion.
corpus.py:256-262: when `create_found` is False, `generation = None` unconditionally — the row is unverified regardless of whether the stored fingerprint matches empty material.

Inverted-trace: if the hardcoded value were stale/wrong (no longer equal to empty-material fingerprint), the test still passes, so it cannot detect a regression that reconstructs missing-CREATE as empty material AND matches — the exact regression the test claims to guard.
advisory.finding: `test_build_corpus_marks_unverified_when_no_create_event_recoverable` hardcodes the 'empty material' fingerprint and never asserts it actually equals `material_fingerprint()` of empty material, so the test stays green even if that premise is false — it does not actually prove the anti-spurious-match guard it names.
scenarios: material_fingerprint normalization changes so the empty-material hash differs; the hardcoded constant goes stale; the test still passes but no longer tests the spurious-match guard.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the hardcoded literal with `empty_material_fingerprint = material_fingerprint(_ctx(ticket_id, ""))` and add `assert manifest` reflects it; this ties the test to the real collision the guard defends against.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish git's 'missing' line from an unparseable header in _batch_cat, and surface (count/raise) dropped or unresolved blobs instead of silently omitting them from `contents`.
evidence: corpus.py:116-123: header parsed, `if len(parts) != 3: continue` before any `proc.stdout.read(size)`
corpus.py:140-142: `raw = bodies.get(b.sha)` / `if raw is None: continue` — a missing body silently drops the event with no counter or warning
The check produces the same result (blob absent from `contents`) whether git returned a genuine 'missing' line or the parse desynced — the failure of the read is invisible.
dropped.finding: In _batch_cat, a header line that does not split into exactly 3 tokens is skipped with `continue`, which consumes the per-sha loop iteration WITHOUT reading a body; if git ever emits a body-bearing line the parser doesn't recognize, subsequent readline() calls read mid-body and the whole batch desyncs, and a dropped blob is silently absent from `contents` (later `bodies.get(b.sha)` returns None and the event is dropped) with no error.
scenarios: A large real tracker where cat-file emits an unexpected header form, or a truncated/short read, silently drops events and lowers verified counts with no diagnostic.
